**1/5 stars — Stackhouse Cloud: support has left our small library stuck**

Bridger Bend Community Library is a one-branch library with two full-time staff members, volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We signed a three-year Stackhouse Cloud contract in June 2026 at $14,200 per year. Our migration went live on October 19.

The software looked good in the demo, and the staff interface is honestly better than our old system. The problem is support. Since October 28, checkouts have worked only offline on one laptop. Around 640 holds disappeared from the queue. We have an open support ticket that has been waiting 12 days; we’ve received three replies, each saying the issue was “escalated to engineering.”

For a small library, these aren’t minor inconveniences. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to pick up his held large-print Westerns. We had no record of the hold and had to send him home without them. One of our volunteers is recording checkouts on index cards while we wait for the system to work again.

We were promised “a dedicated migration specialist.” In practice, we got a shared inbox. I understand that technical problems happen, and I’m not reviewing Stackhouse’s product idea or the quality of the interface. I’m reviewing the gap between the support we were promised and the support we’ve received while basic circulation functions and patron holds are disrupted.

Our county budget hearing is November 18, and our library line item is on the agenda. At $14,200 a year, this contract is a significant commitment for a library our size. I want a named senior person at Stackhouse to call me this week with a clear plan and timeline for restoring service and addressing the lost holds.

For other library directors considering Stackhouse: ask for support response times and escalation commitments in writing before signing, and ask what “dedicated migration specialist” means in practice. The interface may be an improvement, but make sure the support behind it is there when you need it.

One star for now. I would revisit this review if Stackhouse resolves the problems and follows through on support.
